title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1970-09-20
source: Source Info: Master Soundboard Reels (borrowed by Peter Kafer) > Will Boswell's reel @ 7 1/2 ips; Transfer Info: Reel (Technics RS1506) > Tascam DA-3000 (DSF 1bit/5.6 MHz) > dBpoweramp 24/96 > Adobe Audition 3.0 > TLH flac2496

ai_review.summary: Stunning 9/20/70 performance with epic "Cumberland Blues" and "New Speedway Boogie", captured on a clear soundboard tape.
ai_review.review: The show is praised as one of the reviewer’s favorites, highlighted by powerful renditions of “Cumberland Blues”, “New Speedway Boogie” and an emotionally charged “To Lay Me Down”.  The recording, sourced from a sound‑board, is generally clean though a vintage hiss is noted, and the mix lets Tom Constanten’s mournful piano shine alongside Pigpen’s organ.  Overall the musical delivery and audio fidelity combine for a highly enjoyable listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: All five reviews are 4‑5 stars and overwhelmingly positive about both performance and sound quality, giving a strong consensus for a high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Slight vintage hiss noted but overall clear; piano/organ balance is well‑defined, no major dropouts or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical 1970 acoustic/electric blend praised for its seamless transitions and overall energy; reviewers highlight the emotional depth of the second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s vocal delivery is described as solemn and longing; his guitar presence is subtle on this tape.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir is noted for occasional “doing his thing” throughout the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s soft, mournful piano playing receives strong praise and is highlighted as a key element alongside Pigpen’s organ.
